taxonomic_note: Older field guides and nursery sources may still use the former genus Gaura; preserve those names as synonyms but use current Oenothera placement canonically.
look_here_first: Recognize the tall airy perennial first: wiry arching flowering stems carry white-to-pink four-petaled flowers with the petals held mostly toward the upper side and long exserted stamens hanging/projecting below.
project_tracker_diagnostic: perennial clump from a stout rootstock; tall wiry branching stems; narrow lanceolate leaves; four petals oriented mainly to one side/upward side of the flower; 8 long exserted stamens; flowers in an airy elongate spike/raceme

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO gives the native range as southeastern Texas to southwestern Louisiana, not Central Texas. Texas Wildbuds explicitly notes that its Austin/Travis Wildflower Center images are outside the native range and that the species is mainly native in southeastern Texas and southwestern Louisiana. The project source pool has Hays wild observations, but those are not counted as native-range evidence because the species is widely cultivated and can persist/escape outside its native range.

approval_exception.reason: User explicitly approved canonical inclusion despite unresolved target-zone native-range evidence. No target county is inferred or fabricated.

best_field_traits: perennial clump from a stout rootstock
four petals oriented mainly to one side/upward side of the flower

comparisons.key_distinctions: Oenothera suffulta: Both have the old 'gaura' look, but O. lindheimeri is a perennial clumping plant with larger airy flowers and strongly one-sided petal presentation; O. suffulta is an annual with a more compact spike, radial white flowers, crimson anthers, and chunky 4-lobed nutlike fruit. Oenothera curtiflora: O. curtiflora is an annual velveteen plant with extremely tiny flowers (~3 mm across); O. lindheimeri has conspicuous showy flowers and a tall airy perennial habit.
